id: HL-07, HL-08 a section holding a fence is left as written, whatever closes the fence
note: fix() read any ``` or ~~~ line as a fence that opens or closes a block, so a ``` line inside a ~~~ block ended it: an added item 1 went inside the block (HL-08), and a range inside it was listed and published (HL-07). Fences are now read as CommonMark reads them, as move_lines reads them (skills::approvals::fence_lines): a block closes only on a line of its own character, at least as long, with nothing after it. fix() and move_lines rewrite nothing in a section (a ## heading to the next) that holds a line with a run of 3 or more backticks or tildes, a blockquote line or a line indented 4 or more columns that is not a list continuation; such a section keeps 0.1.4 behaviour (the lint blocks, the draft is kept), so no code block is guessed at. The plain range in the same section as the blocks now stays and blocks too. Each refused step also holds a plain range in another section, which publish lists (an ADVISORY line), so a step tells this rule apart from a base without fix() as well as from one that rewrites the code section.
